ai.description: The Sikkim Lazy Toad reaches 4–6 cm. It is brown with dark mottling and a pale belly. Distinctive features include a flattened body, short limbs, and a lack of visible tympanum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Scutiger sikimmensis* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped glandular spines on its chest and limbs, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Sikkim Lazy Toad inhabits high-altitude temperate forests and alpine meadows in the Himalayas, typically found near streams at elevations between 2,000 and 4,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sikkim lazy toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates across the damp forest floors of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Scutiger sikimmensis* breeds in mountain streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to stones.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Scutiger sikimmensis* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within Sikkim and West Bengal, typically inhabiting high-altitude streams between 2,000–4,000m.
ai.callDescription: The Sikkim Lazy Toad emits a series of low-pitched, pulsed croaks, typically heard from hidden positions within fast-flowing mountain streams or rocky seepages.
